thread.title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Poised For Slight Bounce After Monday's Gut-wrenching Reversal

author: morningstar.com
title: MARKET SNAPSHOT: Dow Poised For Slight Bounce After Monday's Gut-wrenching Reversal
text:
By Mark DeCambre, MarketWatch , Chris Matthews
Shares of Dow component Coca-Cola rise after topping Wall Street earnings expectations; Pfizer disappoints on results
Stock-index futures on Monday were set to open slightly higher Tuesday, a day after the Dow Jones Industrial Average staged an ugly reversal to end the session with a triple-digit loss, partly on the back of tariff worries. Comments President Donald Trump made during a late-Monday interview gave investors some hope that the president is ready to make a deal to ease trade tensions with China.
However, fears about global growth and peak earnings continued to persist.
How did major benchmarks fare?
Futures for the Dow were up about 105 points, or 0.4%, at 24,525, those for the S&P 500 index were gaining 13.15 points, or 0.5%, at 2,656.75. Nasdaq-100 futures were gaining 27.75 points, or 0.4%, at 6,764
On Monday, the Dow shed 245.39 points, or 1%, to close at 24,442.92. At its session low, it was down 566 points, and was up as much as 352 points at its intraday peak. The S&P 500 index slid 17.44 points, or 0.7%, to 2,641.25 and the Nasdaq Composite Index dropped 116.92 points, or 1.6%, to 7,050.29.
What is driving the market?
Stocks have entered a decidedly more volatile phase of trade, fueled by myriad concerns, with doubts about the health of the global economy chief among them.
Moreover, shares of companies that have done the most to help drive the U.S. stock market to repeated highs have come off the rails. So-called FAANG names, the acronym referring to technology and internet-related giants Facebook Inc.(FB), Amazon.com Inc. (AMZN), Apple Inc. (AAPL), Netflix Inc.(NFLX) and Google-parent Alphabet Inc. (GOOGL) were all trading sharply lower for October. Amazon.com Inc., on Monday, fell into bear-market territory, wiping out about $120 billion in market value.
The tech-heavy Nasdaq is in correction territory, defined as a drop of at least 10% from a recent peak, while the Dow and S&P 500 are both flirting with tumbling into correction for the second time in 2018.
The market may take a modicum of relief from Trump's late-Monday comments during a Fox News interview, but the president didn't appear to suggest that any deal was imminent. During a Monday interview with Laura Ingraham of Fox News, where he said that the U.S. "will make a great deal with China and it has to be great, because they've drained our country."
Stock losses on Monday accelerated after a Bloomberg report indicated that White House is prepared to announce tariffs on remaining Chinese imports (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/stock-market-turns-negative-amid-report-that-us-set-to-impose-tariffs-on-all-remaining-chinese-imports-2018-10-29) if talks next month between Trump and Xi Jinping don' yield results.
Markets were also digesting a raft of quarterly corporate results. About 430 companies are slated to report results on Tuesday, according to FactSet data.
What stocks were in focus
Shares of General Electric Co. (GE) were rising 0.5% in premarket action after it slashed its dividend (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/ge-slashes-dividend-plans-to-split-up-power-unit-2018-10-30-74852749) and reported disappointing third-quarter results but announced a restructuring of its power business.
Shares of Coca-Cola Co. (KO) rose 1.2% in premarket trade Tuesday, after the beverage and snack giant reported third-quarter earnings and revenue that topped expectations (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/coca-colas-stock-gains-after-earnings-and-revenue-rise-above-expectations-2018-10-30).
Pfizer Inc.'s stock (PFE)fell 3.5% before the bell Tuesday, after the pharmaceutical giant reported third-quarter earnings (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/pfizers-stock-falls-after-profit-beats-but-revenue-misses-2018-10-30) that beat expectations but revenue that missed, and provided a downbeat revenue outlook.
Shares of cloud services firm Akamai Technologies, Inc. (AKAM) were up 10.3% before the bell Tuesday, after the firm beat third-quarter estimates and raised its fourth-quarter guidance and full-year outlook in an earnings release Monday evening.
Under Armour, Inc. (UAA) stock was up 9.7% in premarket trading, after the company announced third-quarter earnings and revenue (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/shares-of-under-armour-up-94-after-earnings-beat-2018-10-30) that beat analysts' estimates.
Shares in Cognizant Technology Corp. (CTSH) were falling 10.3%, after the technology-services firm said its profit fell in the third-quarter, year-over-year, falling short of analysts expectations.
Masco Corp. (MAS) shares are falling 6% in premarket action after missing analysts profit estimates in a Tuesday morning earnings announcement.
Separately, Chesapeake Energy Corp. (CHK) were down 11.3% after it announced (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/chesapeake-energy-to-acquire-wildhorse-in-cash-and-stock-deal-valued-at-about-4-billion-2018-10-30) that it would acquire WildHorse Resource Development Corp. (WRD) in a cash-and-stock deal valued at $4 billion. WildHorse share are up 7.2% in premarket action.
Several big-name companies are set to report earnings after the bell, including Facebook, Inc.(FB), e-Bay, Inc. (EBAY), and MGM Resorts International(MGM).
What are analysts saying?
"The futures are pointing to a bounce at the opening after yesterdays swings, suggesting another similar session is in the makings. Nevertheless, we think we are getting very close to the end of the correction," wrote Peter Cardillo, chief market economist at Spartan Capital Securities, in a Tuesday research note.
"We look for consumers confidence to slip as the markets decline impacts putting the index at 132. Weaker home prices are expected as the S&P Case-Shiller index rises a slim 0.2%."
What data were in focus?
After the opening bell, the Case-Shiller home price index for August is set to be released at 9 a.m. Eastern Time. At 10 a.m., reports on consumer confidence for October and home ownership are scheduled.
How were other markets trading?
Asian markets finished higher on the day, European stocks were mostly lower as the Stoxx Europe 600 (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/italian-stocks-lead-europe-markets-higher-banks-auto-names-climb-2018-10-29) (http://www.marketwatch.com/story/italian-stocks-lead-europe-markets-higher-banks-auto-names-climb-2018-10-29)traded off 0.1% but the U.K. FTSE 100 climbed 0.2%.
Oil futures looked set to extend their losses. Gold traded lower, while the U.S. dollar weakened.
